text:
harper: Quick RFC follow-up — how should the gateway handle a mid-stream failure and fallback to a sync endpoint? thinking about token checkpoint + client resume vs. immediate close-and-retry. looking for concrete handshake + policy suggestions.

maya: My take: prefer resume if client supports it. preserves partial output and avoids duplicate token costs. downside = more state and complexity at the edge.

tom: +1 on resume but clients must opt-in. otherwise we risk clients waiting on a stream that will never resume. need explicit `Idempotency-Key` and resume acceptance.

oli: rough protocol sketch: gateway issues ephemeral resume token header when stream is cut. client can call sync/resume endpoint with that token. Fallback path returns a `410` or `409` with `X-Resume-Token` and small JSON describing resume window. Example headers/response:

```
HTTP/1.1 409 StreamInterrupted
Content-Type: application/json
X-Resume-Token: eyJvIjoicGFydGlhbC10b2tlbiIsImV4cCI6MTg5ODc2NTQ5Mn0=
Stream-State: partial

{
  "reason": "edge_connection_reset",
  "resume_window_ms": 30000,
  "resume_supported": true
}
```

maya: Also include `X-Fallback-Model` if we transparently switch to a cheaper/non-streaming model mid-request. that way clients can log and decide.

tom: Operational concerns: storing resume tokens per-request -> memory pressure. proposal: only keep tokens for TTL=30s and limit to N active tokens per-edge node. if TTL expires we return `410 Gone`.

oli: To reduce state, we can encode minimal state into the token (signed, encrypted): model, prefix-kv-checkpoint-id, last-ack-seq. then gateway can validate without full KV. but this limits how much recovery we can do.

harper: Good point. tradeoff: encoded token (stateless) vs server-side ephemeral (more control). which should be default?

maya: Default = encoded token + short TTL (30s) to avoid referral to external store. Option to opt into server-side persisted tokens for enterprise tenants who want stronger guarantees.

sre-bot: Observability reqs: emit `edge.resume_token.created`, `edge.resume_attempt`, `edge.resume_success`, `edge.fallback_to_sync`, and `edge.resume_token.expired`. Tag by tenant_id + model. Also trace id link in token.

tom: Retry accounting: any resume attempt should draw from the request's retry budget. if resume fails we should not silently retry infinitely. cap resume attempts per-request (default 1).

oli: Backpressure interactions: when client resumes, we need to re-establish KV-cache window for attention states. if we encoded a `last_ack_seq` the runtime can replay tokens from that seq. otherwise fallback to full re-generation.

harper: Regarding billing: do we charge for tokens emitted before abort + tokens generated during resume? need explicit policy. suggestion: charge for successful output only; failed partial tokens covered under SLA or internal budget.

maya: billing aside, we should surface clearly to clients: `x-fallback-model: gptx-small` and `x-resume-available: true|false` on abort. clients can choose to call resume endpoint or restart.

tom: config example (edge routing / policy):

```json
{
  "fallback_policy": "resume-first", // options: resume-first | sync-first | always-sync
  "resume_ttl_ms": 30000,
  "max_resume_attempts": 1,
  "resume_token_mode": "signed-compact" // options: signed-compact | server-ephemeral
}
```

harper: Security note: resume tokens must be signed and single-use to avoid replay. include tenant scope and trace id.

sre-bot: Perf note: if we see >0.5% of streams issuing resume tokens on a node, escalate — that indicates instability.

deploy-bot: Heads up — can we get a staging rollout to validate resume token flow? I can schedule a canary for tomorrow 09:00 PT. :calendar: 

harper: Next steps I volunteer to draft the RFC follow-up: handshake headers, token format (signed compact), TTL=30s default, metrics, and operator defaults. will add a section on opt-in server-side persistence for enterprise.

maya: :thumbsup: add a small client example for `resume` call so SDKs can implement.

oli: I'll prototype minimal token encoding and a validation lib.

tom: I'll add retry budget enforcement in the gateway and a config flag to disable resume if tenants prefer simpler semantics.

harper: Thanks all — will open PR with concrete headers and example responses.
